hints: Ask yourself what both a bacterial cell and your own cells must do every minute: make proteins. What three RNA helpers does translation always need?
Remember the three jobs: mRNA carries the gene copy, rRNA builds the ribosome, tRNA delivers amino acids. If both cell types have ribosomes, which RNAs must both have?
walkthrough:
**Start with what both cells share**

Both prokaryotic cells and eukaryotic cells carry out protein synthesis. That means both need the full translation machinery to read genes and build polypeptides.

**Match each RNA to its essential job**

Think of the team: mRNA is the messenger copy of a gene, rRNA forms the structure of the ribosome where the protein is built, and tRNA brings the correct amino acids to the ribosome. No cell can translate without all three working together.

**Conclude for both cell types**

Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes and eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes, but both are made of rRNA and both use mRNA and tRNA in exactly the same way. So mRNA, rRNA and tRNA are all present in both. That is option A.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes translate mRNA on rRNA ribosomes using tRNA, so all three RNAs are present.
options.B: Not quite. tRNA is essential in prokaryotes too to deliver amino acids during translation, so it cannot be absent.
options.C: Not quite. Prokaryotes definitely make mRNA by transcription of their DNA, they just do it in the cytoplasm without a nucleus.
options.D: Not quite. Only rRNA being present would mean no message to read and no amino acid carriers, so protein synthesis would be impossible.
